text:
Alex Ovechkin has one goal in 18 games, and TSN has pointed out that he's on pace for about five goals in what's billed as his final season. He hasn't scored in 13 games. For the greatest goal scorer the league has seen, now 41 with 930 career goals, it's a strange way for things to look.

Our numbers say the drought is mostly bad luck. Over his last ten games he's had 3.8 expected goals (the quality of chances) on his own shots, more than his recent usual of 2.8. For the season, he has 1 goal on 5.2 expected. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile for chances from the slot last season, when he scored 32. He's still getting there. The pucks aren't going in.

The real change is the role: 13:37 a night, and Washington takes 52% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, a bit below the team rate. Our talent range still projects around 18 goals, which would mean a lot of them still to come. With nine Rocket Richard trophies and three Harts behind him, nobody needs to explain who he is. The question is whether the finish returns in time.
